<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><a style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On June 14, 2013, CNG, SCG and Yankee Gas Services Company, an unrelated regulated gas distribution company, filed a comprehensive joint 10 year natural gas expansion plan (&#8220;Expansion Plan&#8221;) with PURA and DEEP. The plan was in response to the gas expansion goals proposed in the Connecticut Governor&#8217;s Comprehensive Energy Strategy and Public Act 13-298.&#160; The Expansion Plan included a set of recommendations designed to help meet the statewide goal of adding approximately 280,000 new customers, including providing more flexibility to minimize a new customer&#8217;s contribution to the cost to serve them, providing tools to help fund natural gas conversion costs, establishing a process to extend natural gas service for interested customers who are further away from the main gas line, and&#160; allowing utilities to secure additional pipeline capacity coming into Connecticut.&#160; PURA issued its final Decision on November 22, 2013.&#160; In this decision PURA approved new System Expansion (SE) rates exclusively for new on and off-main customers commencing service on or after January 1, 2014.&#160; These rates include a 10% premium distribution component for on-main customers and a 30% premium for off-main customers.&#160; The SE rates are complemented by new business rules that extend the Companies&#8217; financial hurdle rate model from a 20-year to a 25-year time horizon, which will reduce the customer&#8217;s contributions to any construction costs, and allow the grouping of customers to help reduce or eliminate new customer contributions to system expansion.&#160; A separate new business reconciliation mechanism is also approved that reconciles the actual new business revenue requirements each year with the revenues received from the new business customers.&#160;&#160; As a result of the reconciliation, any shortfall or surplus in revenues will be charged or credited to existing firm customers.&#160; This ensures the timely recovery of new business capital investments and any associated expenses.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Gas Supply Arrangements</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><!--Anchor--><!--Anchor--><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gas </font>Companies<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> satisfy their natural gas supply requirements through purchases from various producer/suppliers, withdrawals from natural gas storage capacity contracts and winter peaking supplies and resources.&#160; The Gas </font>Companies<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> operate diverse portfolios of gas supply, firm transportation capacity, gas storage and peaking resources.&#160; Actual reasonable gas costs incurred by each of the Gas </font>Companies<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> are passed through to customers through state regulated purchased gas adjustment mechanisms, subject to regulatory review.</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gas Companies purchase the majority of their natural gas supply at market prices under seasonal, monthly or mid-term supply contracts and the remainder is acquired on the spot market.&#160; The Gas </font>Companies<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> diversify their sources of supply by amount purchased and location. The Gas Companies primarily acquire gas at various locations in the US Gulf of Mexico region, in the Appalachia region and in Canada.</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gas Companies acquire firm transportation capacity on interstate pipelines under long-term contracts and utilize that capacity to transport both natural gas supply purchased and natural gas withdrawn from storage to the local distribution system.&#160; Collectively, the Gas Companies hold approximately 100 firm transportation contracts on 12 different pipelines.&#160; Three of those pipelines, Tennessee Gas Pipeline, Algonquin Gas Transmission and Iroquois Gas Transmission, interconnect with one or more of the Gas </font>Companies&#8217; distribution system<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> and the other pipelines provide indirect services upstream of the city gates.&#160; The prices and terms and conditions of the long-term contracts for firm transportation capacity are regulated by the FERC.&#160; The actual reasonable costs of such contracts are passed through to customers through state regulated purchased gas adjustment mechanisms.</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gas Companies acquire firm underground natural gas storage capacity using long-term contracts and fill the storage facilities with gas in the summer months for subsequent withdrawal in the winter months.&#160; Collectively, the Gas </font>Companies<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> hold 24 gas storage contracts with seven different storage contractors.&#160; The storage facilities are located in Pennsylvania, New York, West Virginia and Michigan.</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Winter peaking resources are primarily attached to the local distribution systems and are either owned or are contracted for by the Gas </font>Companies, each of which is a <font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Local Distribution Company.&#160; Each Gas Company owns or has rights to the natural gas stored in a Liquefied Natural Gas facility directly attached to its distribution system.</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Cash Flows</u></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Cash flows provided by operating activities totaled $325.2 million in 2013, compared with $333.9 million in 2012.&#160; The decrease in operating cash flows was related primarily to changes in taxes accrued/refundable, accounts receivable and natural gas in storage.&#160; The decrease in cash flows from changes in taxes accrued/refundable is primarily due to the absence in 2013 of tax refunds received in 2012 of approximately $65.8 million resulting from an accounting change for tax purposes as well as a federal income tax refund generated by the carryback of a portion of UIL Holdings&#8217; 2011 net operating loss to the 2009 and 2010 tax years.&#160; The increase in cash flows from changes in accounts receivable and the decrease in cash flows from changes in natural gas in storage are directly correlated to increases in sales, primarily related to gas distribution volume, in the fourth quarter of 2012 as compared to the fourth quarter of 2011.&#160; Given that November and December are the beginning of the gas winter heating season, gas distribution sales in the fourth quarter help drive cash collections and the need for gas inventory purchases in the first quarter of the following year.<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </font>This increase in sales in the fourth quarter was primarily due to the colder weather in the fourth quarter of 2012 as compared to the fourth quarter of 2011.&#160;&#160; Temperatures were 10.5% colder in the fourth quarter of 2012 as compared to the fourth quarter of 2011 which resulted in an increase of 551 heating degree days in the fourth quarter of 2012.&#160; The gas distribution business had operating revenue of $226.2 million in the fourth quarter of 2012 compared to $178.3 million in the fourth quarter of 2011.&#160; Retail gas sales increased by 3.3 million mcf in the fourth quarter of 2012 when compared to the fourth quarter of 2011.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings expects to fund capital requirements that exceed available cash through external financings.&#160; Although there is currently no commitment to provide such financing from any source of funds, other than from the financings and credit facilities discussed below, UIL Holdings expects to satisfy future external financing needs by the issuance of additional equity and/or short&#8209;term and long&#8209;term debt.&#160; The continued availability and timing of such financings will be dependent on many factors, including conditions in the bank and capital markets, general economic conditions and UIL Holdings&#8217; future income and cash flow.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition to the covenants described in &#8220;&#8211; Liquidity and Capital Resources &#8211; Financial Covenants&#8221;, the following potential restrictions on the payment of dividends by UIL Holdings&#8217; subsidiaries exist under law, contractual provisions and a charter provision:</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Federal Power Act declares it to be unlawful for any officer or director of any public utility &#8220;to participate&#8221; in the making or paying of any dividends of such public utility from any funds properly included in capital account.&#8221;&#160; This restriction would apply to UI.&#160; FERC has consistently interpreted the provision to allow dividends to be paid as long as (1) the source of the dividends is clearly disclosed, (2) the dividend is not excessive and (3) there is no self-dealing on the part of corporate officials.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Corporate laws in the states in which we operate, Connecticut and Massachusetts, authorize distributions to the extent they are not limited by corporate documents such as charters and bylaws and do not result in insolvency.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Provisions in the Certificate of Incorporation of CNG require that dividends on its $3.125 Par Preferred Stock be paid before dividends may be paid on the common stock.&#160; On February 3, 2014, CNG announced an offer to purchase all of the issued and outstanding shares of CNG&#8217;s $3.125 Par Preferred Stock for a purchase price of $7.50 per share.&#160; The offer to purchase will expire on March 4, 2014.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management does not believe any of these restrictions meaningfully impair the subsidiaries&#8217; ability to pay dividends&#160;&#160; because the restrictions have not prevented the subsidiaries from paying dividends in an amount sufficient to meet UIL Holdings&#8217; dividend and debt service needs, even taking into account such limitations.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Financial Covenants</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings and its subsidiaries are required to comply with certain covenants in connection with their respective loan agreements.&#160; We believe that the covenants are normal and customary.&#160; The summary below describes the most significant financial covenants, certain events of default and dividend restrictions in the agreements.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Long-Term Debt</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The long-term debt agreements describe typical events of default, including the situation in which the borrower defaults on indebtedness in the aggregate principal amount of at least $1 million, $5 million or $10 million due to (i) a default in payment or payments due on the indebtedness, or (ii) default in the performance of or compliance with any term or condition of the indebtedness, which could result in the requirement that such indebtedness be repaid, or (iii) the occurrence of any event or condition that could require the purchase or repayment of the indebtedness prior to maturity.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>UI</u></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><!--Anchor--><!--Anchor-->Under each of its taxable long-term debt agreements, UI is required to maintain a ratio of consolidated debt to consolidated capital of not greater than 65% (debt ratio).&#160; As of December 31, 2013, UI&#8217;s debt ratio was 52%. For additional information on UI&#8217;s taxable long-term debt agreements, see Part II, Item 8, &#8220;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data &#8211; Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements &#8211; Note (B), Capitalization,&#8221; of this Form 10-K.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There are no dividend restrictions in connection with the above agreements absent an event of default.&#160;&#160; In addition, there are no repayment triggers specified in the above agreements related to changes in debt ratings.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Gas Companies</u></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under the Note Purchase Agreement in connection with the $15,000,000 principal amount of 5.33% Senior Notes, Series A, due December 10, 2043 between Berkshire and various Accredited Investors, Berkshire is required to maintain a ratio of consolidated debt to consolidated capital of not greater than 65% (debt ratio).&#160; As of December 31, 2013, Berkshire&#8217;s debt ratio was 29%.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under the Amended and Restated Note Agreement in connection with the 7.8% Senior Unsecured Note, due&#160; November 15, 2021, in the original principal amount of $16 million, Berkshire is required to maintain a ratio of consolidated funded debt to consolidated adjusted capitalization of not greater than 65%.&#160; As of December 31, 2013, such ratio was 43.7% (adjusted capitalization excludes the impact of goodwill).&#160; In addition, Berkshire is required to maintain a fixed charges coverage ratio of no less than 1.50 to 1.00.&#160; As of December 31, 2013, such ratio was 4.79 to 1.00.&#160; The Amended and Restated Note Agreement describes typical events of default, including the situation in which Berkshire defaults on any payment required in connection with the Amended and Restated Note Agreement or on any other indebtedness in the aggregate principal amount of at least $1 million.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under the Indenture in connection with the 10.06% First Mortgage Bond Series P, due February 1, 2019, in the principal amount of $10 million, Berkshire is required to maintain a fixed charge ratio of at least 2.00 to 1.00.&#160; As of December 31, 2013, Berkshire&#8217;s fixed charge ratio was 4.87 to 1.00.&#160; Pursuant to the Indenture, Berkshire is also subject to cash dividend, distribution and common stock share purchase restrictions if the aggregate amount of such dividends, distributions and purchases exceeds Berkshire's earned surplus, plus $3 million.&#160; During 2013, there were no such dividends, distributions and purchases in excess of such limitation.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><!--Anchor--><!--Anchor--><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SCG is subject to dividend restrictions pursuant to the terms of all of its senior secured notes.&#160; The most limiting of these dividend restrictions relates to the most recently issued notes, which are the </font>3.88% medium-term notes, due September 22, 2021, in the principal amount of $25 million, the secured 5.39% medium-term notes, due September 22, 2041, in the principal amount of $25 million, Series MTN-IV, constituting a series of first mortgage bonds<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> and the 7.5% Senior Secured Medium Term Note IV in the principal amount of $50.0 million, due 2018, all of which were issued under SCG's Thirty-First Supplemental Indenture.&#160; </font>The restrictions are based upon cumulative net income available for dividends since January 1, 2008, plus $60 million, offset by adjustments related to aggregate depreciation expense and dividends declared.<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160; </font><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2013, $76.2 million was unrestricted for dividend distributions.</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Short-term Debt</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings has a $400 million credit facility under which UIL Holdings, UI, SCG, CNG and Berkshire are each required to maintain a ratio of consolidated debt to consolidated capital of not greater than 65% (debt ratio).&#160; As of December 31, 2013, UIL Holdings&#8217; debt ratio was 56%, UI&#8217;s debt ratio was 52%, SCG&#8217;s debt ratio was 36%, CNG&#8217;s debt ratio was 30% and Berkshire&#8217;s debt ratio was 29%.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The credit facility describes typical events of default, including the situation in which the borrower fails to pay when due any interest or principal due on indebtedness in the principal amount of at least $10 million or any interest or premium thereon in the aggregate amount of at least $10 million; or any other default or other event shall occur related to such indebtedness if the effect of such default or event is to accelerate, or to permit the acceleration of, the maturity of such indebtedness, or any such indebtedness shall be declared due and payable, or required to be prepaid, prior to the stated maturity.&#160; Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the foregoing, a default by UIL Holdings generally does not create a cross-default in respect of outstanding indebtedness of UI, SCG, CNG or Berkshire (except in the case of a default arising from a Change of Control of UIL Holdings, as defined in the <font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">credit facility</font>).</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There are no dividend restrictions in connection with the credit facility.&#160;&#160; In addition, there are no automatic repayments specified in the credit facility related to changes in debt ratings.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">2014 Capital Resource and Expenditure Projections</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For financial planning purposes, the amount of UIL Holdings&#8217; quarterly per share cash dividend in 2014 is currently projected to be equal to the cash dividend of $0.432 per share paid in each quarter of 2013.&#160; UIL Holdings will continue to be dependent on dividends from its subsidiaries and from external borrowings to provide the cash in excess of the amount currently on hand that is necessary for debt service, to pay administrative costs, and to pay common stock dividends to UIL Holdings&#8217; shareowners.&#160; As UIL Holdings&#8217; sources of cash are limited to cash on hand, dividends from its subsidiaries and external capital raising activities, the ability to maintain future cash dividends at the level currently paid to shareowners will be dependent primarily upon sustained earnings from current operations of UI and the Gas Companies.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In order to achieve long-term growth in earnings, UI and the Gas Companies will likely need to increase their rate base through distribution, transmission and transportation reliability and capacity enhancement capital investment programs.&#160; If additions to the rate base and returns on equity investments are lower than the annual amount of depreciation and amortization, the earnings of UI and the Gas Companies may decline.&#160; See &#8220;&#8211;Major Influences on Financial Condition&#8221; for more information.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings expects to incur capital expenditures of approximately $376 million.&#160; Additional cash requirements in excess of cash flows generated from operating activities are expected to be funded by short-term debt.</div>

<div><br>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="CRITICALACCOUNTING"><!--Anchor--></a>CRITICAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings&#8217; Consolidated Financial Statements are prepared based on certain critical accounting policies that require management to make judgments and estimates that are subject to varying degrees of uncertainty.&#160; Investors need to be aware of these policies and how they impact UIL Holdings&#8217; financial reporting to gain a more complete understanding of UIL Holdings&#8217; Consolidated Financial Statements as a whole, as well as management&#8217;s related discussion and analysis presented herein.&#160; While UIL Holdings believes that these accounting policies are grounded on sound measurement </div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">criteria, actual future events can and often do result in outcomes that can be materially different from these estimates or forecasts.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Accounting for Regulated Public Utilities</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America (GAAP) allow regulated entities to give accounting recognition to the actions of regulatory authorities in accordance with the provisions of the ASC 980 &#8220;Regulated Operations.&#8221;&#160; In order to apply such regulatory accounting treatment and record regulatory assets and liabilities, certain criteria must be met.&#160; In determining whether the criteria are met for its operations, UIL Holdings&#8217; management makes significant judgments, which involve (i) determining whether rates for services provided to customers are subject to approval by an independent, third-party regulator, (ii) determining whether the regulated rates are designed to recover specific costs of providing the regulated service, (iii) considering relevant historical precedents and recent decisions of the regulatory authorities and (iv) considering the fact that decisions made by<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>regulatory commissions or legislative changes at a later date could vary from earlier interpretations made by management and that the impact of such variations<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>could be material.&#160; In accordance with ASC 980, UIL Holdings&#8217; regulated subsidiaries have deferred recognition of costs (a regulatory asset) or have recognized obligations (a regulatory liability) if it is probable that such costs will be recovered or obligations relieved in the future through the ratemaking process.&#160; In addition to the Regulatory Assets and Liabilities identified on the Consolidated Balance Sheet, and in Part II, Item 8, &#8220;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data &#8211; Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements &#8211; Note (A) &#8211; Regulatory Accounting,&#8221; there are other regulatory assets and liabilities included in the Consolidated Balance Sheet such as certain deferred tax assets and liabilities.&#160; UIL Holdings&#8217; regulated subsidiaries also have obligations under power contracts, the recovery of which is subject to regulation.&#160; Management regularly reviews its regulatory assets<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>and liabilities to determine whether adjustments to its previous conclusions are necessary based on the current regulatory and legislative environment as well<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>as recent rate orders.<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </font>If UIL Holdings&#8217; regulated subsidiaries, or a portion of their assets or operations, were to cease meeting the criteria for application of these accounting rules, accounting standards for businesses in general would become applicable and immediate recognition of any previously deferred costs would be required in the year in which such criteria are no longer met (if such deferred costs are not recoverable in the portion of the business that continues to meet the criteria for application of ASC 980).</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Accounting for Pensions and Other Postretirement Benefits</div>

<div><br>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings accounts for its pension and postretirement benefit plans in accordance with ASC 715 &#8220;Compensation </font>&#8211;<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Retirement Benefits.&#8221;</font><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </font><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In applying these accounting practices, assumptions are made regarding the valuation of benefit obligations and the performance of plan assets.&#160; Delayed recognition of differences between actual results and those assumed allows for a smoother recognition of changes in benefit obligations and plan performance over the working lives of the employees who benefit under the plans.&#160; The primary assumptions are as follows:</font></div>

</div>

<td style="WIDTH: 18pt"></td>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; align: right">&#183;</td>
<td style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; WIDTH: auto; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">Expected return on plan assets &#8211; the expected return is based upon a combination of historical performance and anticipated future returns for a portfolio reflecting the mix of equity, debt and other investments included in plan assets.</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">
<table style="WIDTH: 100%; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<tr>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt"></td>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; align: right">&#183;</td>
<td style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; WIDTH: auto; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">Average wage increase &#8211; projected annual pay increases, which are used to determine the wage base used to project employees&#8217; pension benefits at retirement.</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">
<table style="WIDTH: 100%; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<tr>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt"></td>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; align: right">&#183;</td>
<td style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; WIDTH: auto; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">Health care cost trend rate &#8211; projections of expected increases in health care costs.</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">These assumptions are the responsibility of management, in consultation with its outside actuarial and investment advisors.&#160; A variance in the discount rate, expected return on assets or average wage increase could have a significant impact on pension costs, assets and obligations recorded under ASC 715.&#160; In addition to a change in the discount rate and the expected return on assets, a variance in the health care cost trend assumption could have a significant impact on postretirement medical expense recorded under ASC 715.</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div id="DSPFPageFooter"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">- 41 -</div>

<hr style="BORDER-RIGHT-WIDTH: 0px; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #000000; PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; BORDER-TOP-WIDTH: 0px; BORDER-BOTTOM-WIDTH: 0px; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both; BORDER-LEFT-WIDTH: 0px" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">
<div><a style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings applies consistent estimation techniques regarding its actuarial assumptions, where appropriate, across the pension and postretirement plans of its operating subsidiaries.&#160; The estimation technique utilized to develop the discount rate for its pension and postretirement benefit plans is based upon the settlement of such liabilities as of December 31, 2013 utilizing a hypothetical portfolio of actual, high quality bonds, which would generate cash flows required to settle the liabilities.&#160; UIL Holdings believes such an estimate of the discount rate accurately reflects the settlement value for plan obligations and results in cash flows which closely match the expected payments to participants.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings is utilizing a discount rate of 5.20% as of December 31, 2013 for all of its qualified pension plans, compared to a rate of 4.25% in 2012.&#160; The increase in the discount rate, which was due to changes in long-term interest rates, resulted in a decrease to the projected benefit obligation of approximately $100 million from 2012 to 2013.&#160; The discount rate for non-qualified pension plans as of December 31, 2013 was 4.9% compared to 4.0% in 2012.&#160; The discount rates for UIL Holdings&#8217; other postretirement benefits plans reflects the differing plan requirements and expected future cash flows.&#160; For the UI other postretirement plan, the discount rate at December 31, 2013 was 5.20% compared to 4.25% at December 31, 2012.&#160; For the Gas Companies&#8217; other postretirement plans, the December 31, 2013 discount rate is a composite rate of 4.85% compared to 4.0% the previous year.&#160; UIL Holdings&#8217; expected return on plan assets ranged from 5.56% to 8.0% in 2013 and 2012.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The assumptions listed above may be revised over time as economic and market conditions change.&#160; Changes in those assumptions could have a material impact on pension and other postretirement expenses.&#160; For example, if there had been a 0.25% change in the discount rate assumed for the pension plans, the 2013 pension expense would have increased or decreased inversely by $2.6 million.&#160; If there had been a 1% change in the expected return on assets assumed for the pension plans, the 2013 pension expense would have increased or decreased inversely by $6.9 million.&#160;&#160; </font>If there had been a 0.25% change in the discount rate assumed for the other postretirement benefits plans, the 2013 other postretirement benefits plan expenses would have <font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">increased or decreased inversely by </font>$0.3 million.&#160; I<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">f there had been a 1% change in the expected return on assets assumed for the </font>other postretirement benefits plans<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">, the 2013 </font>other postretirement benefits plan<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> expenses would have increased or decreased inversely by $0.4 million.</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The projected, long&#8209;term average wage increases ranged from 3.5% to 3.8% in 2013.&#160; The health care cost trend rate assumption for all retirees was set at 7.5% in 2013, with such rate decreasing by 0.5% per year to 5.0% in 2019.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings&#8217; 2013 pension and other postretirement benefits expenses were </font>$41.4 million and $7.4<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">million, respectively, net of amounts deferred as a regulatory asset.</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The assumptions are used to predict the net periodic expense on a forward-looking basis.&#160; To the extent actual investment earnings, actual wage increases and other items differ from the assumptions, a gain or loss is created, and subsequently amortized into expense.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings reflects all unrecognized prior service costs and credits and unrecognized actuarial gains and losses as regulatory assets as it is probable that such items will be recovered through the ratemaking process in future periods.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Accounting for Contingencies</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ASC 450 &#8220;Contingencies&#8221; applies to an existing condition, situation or set of circumstances involving uncertainty as to possible loss that will ultimately be resolved when one or more future events occur or fail to occur.&#160; In accordance with ASC 450, UIL Holdings accrues estimated losses related to each contingency as to which a loss is probable and can be reasonably estimated; no liability is accrued for any contingency as to which a loss is not probable or cannot be reasonably estimated.&#160; With respect to amounts accrued for contingencies related to UIL Holdings&#8217; regulated subsidiaries, if it is probable that such estimated costs will be recovered through the ratemaking process, recognition of such costs is deferred in accordance with the provisions of ASC 980 (see &#8220;Accounting for Regulated Public Entities &#8211; ASC 980&#8221; of this item).&#160; Refer to Part II, Item 8, &#8220;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data &#8211; Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements &#8211; Note (J), Commitments and Contingencies&#8221; of this Form 10-K for a detailed discussion of UIL Holdings&#8217; current known material contingencies.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Goodwill</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Pursuant to the authoritative guidance on goodwill and other intangible assets, goodwill is not amortized; rather, impairment tests are performed at least annually or more frequently if circumstances indicate an impairment may have occurred.&#160; If an impairment exists, the goodwill is immediately written down to its fair value through a current charge to income.&#160; Accordingly, goodwill is subject to an impairment test at least annually.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The fair market value of each of UIL Holdings&#8217; applicable reporting units is estimated using certain key assumptions that require significant judgment.&#160; This judgment includes developing cash flow projections (including the selection of appropriate returns on equity, long-term growth rates, and capital expenditure levels), selecting appropriate discount rates, and identifying relevant market comparables.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings completed its annual goodwill impairment tests for all of its reporting units that carry a goodwill balance as of October 1, 2013.&#160; The estimated fair values for the reporting units were determined by using the income approach and the market approach methodologies.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The income approach was based on discounted cash flows which were derived from internal forecasts and economic expectations.&#160; Key assumptions used to determine fair value under the income approach included the cash flow period, terminal values based on a terminal growth rate, and the discount rate.&#160; The discount rate represents the estimated cost of debt and equity financing weighted by the percentage of debt and equity in a company's target capital structure.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The market approach utilized the guideline company method, which calculates valuation multiples based on operating and valuation metrics from publicly traded guideline companies in the regulated natural gas distribution industry.&#160; Multiples derived from the guideline companies provided an indication of how much a knowledgeable investor in the marketplace would be willing to pay for an investment in a similar company.&#160; These multiples were then applied to the appropriate operating metric to determine indications of fair value.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of October 1, 2013, the fair values of UIL Holdings&#8217; applicable reporting units exceeded their carrying values and therefore no impairment was recognized.&#160; No events or circumstances occurred subsequent to October 1, 2013 that would make it more likely than not that the fair value of the reporting units fell below their respective carrying values.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="OFF-BALANCESHEET"><!--Anchor--></a>OFF-BALANCE SHEET ARRANGEMENTS</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings occasionally enters into guarantee contracts in the ordinary course of business.&#160; At the time a guarantee is provided, an analysis is performed to assess the expected financial impact, if any, based on the likelihood of certain events occurring that would require UIL Holdings to perform under such guarantee.&#160; Subsequent analysis is performed on a periodic basis to assess the impact of any changes in events or circumstances.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2013, UIL Holdings had certain immaterial guarantee contracts outstanding for which no liability has been recorded in the Consolidated Financial Statements.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings reviews new accounting standards to determine the expected financial impact, if any, that the adoption of each such standard will have.&#160; As of the filing of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, there were no new accounting standards issued that were projected to have a material impact on UIL Holdings&#8217; consolidated financial position, results of operations or liquidity.&#160; Refer to Part II, Item 8, &#8220;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data &#8211; Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements &#8211; Note (A), Statement of Accounting Policies &#8211; New Accounting Standards,&#8221; for further discussion regarding new accounting standards.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Within the &#8220;Results of Operations&#8221; section of this Form 10-K, tabular presentations showing a comparison of UIL Holdings&#8217; net income and earnings per share (EPS) for 2013 and 2012, as well as 2012 and 2011, are provided, along with reconciliations for certain non-GAAP measures.&#160; The amounts presented show the EPS for each of UIL Holdings&#8217; lines of business, as well as EPS excluding the impact of regulatory disallowances, which is calculated by dividing the income of each line of business and the net income of each line of business excluding the regulatory disallowances, by the average number of shares of UIL Holdings&#8217; common stock outstanding for the periods presented.&#160; UIL Holdings believes this information is useful in understanding the fluctuations in EPS between the current and prior year periods.</div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Electric Distribution and Transmission</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Overall, UI&#8217;s operating revenue increased by $20.1 million, from $783.5 million in 2012 to $803.6 million in 2013.&#160; Retail revenue increased $44.4 million, which was primarily attributable to increases in distribution rates, as a result of the 2013 rate case decision, partially offset by decreases in sales volume in 2013 compared to 2012.&#160; Retail sales decreased by 9 million kWh, from 5,431 million kWh in 2012, to 5,422 million kWh in 2013.&#160; Retail sales normalized for the weather impact decreased 36 million kWh, from 5,411 million kWh in 2012, to 5,375 million kWh in 2013.&#160; Other revenues decreased $24.3 million, which was primarily attributable to lower transmission revenue requirements as required to achieve the authorized return, which do not directly impact net income.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Purchased power expense decreased by $15.4 million, from $154.5 million in 2012 to $139.1 million in 2013.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to decreased costs of procured power as well as decreases in sales volume.&#160; UI receives electricity to satisfy its standard service and supplier of last resort requirements through fixed&#8209;price purchased power agreements.&#160; The variance does not impact net income as these costs are recovered through the GSC and Bypassable Federally Mandated Congestion Charges portions of UI&#8217;s unbundled retail customer rates.</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div id="DSPFPageFooter"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">- 44 -</div>

<hr style="BORDER-RIGHT-WIDTH: 0px; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #000000; PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; BORDER-TOP-WIDTH: 0px; BORDER-BOTTOM-WIDTH: 0px; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both; BORDER-LEFT-WIDTH: 0px" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">
<div><a style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UI&#8217;s O&amp;M expense increased by $12.9 million, from $222.0 million in 2012 to $234.9 million in 2013.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to increased employee pension and benefits expense, increased outside services expenses as well as increased system and infrastructure maintenance expenses, partially offset by a decrease in in uncollectible accounts and a decrease in rent expense due to a reduction in office space utilized by UIL Holdings.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UI&#8217;s transmission wholesale expenses increased by $8.7 million, from $79.5 million in 2012 to $88.2 million in 2013.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to higher regional transmission expenses, of which UI pays a portion based upon its relative load and which are recoverable through rates<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> and, as a result, does not impact net income.</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Depreciation and amortization expense increased by $4.4 million, from $103.6 million in 2012 to $108.0 million in 2013. The increase was primarily attributable to increased depreciation due to increases in plant and equipment.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Taxes other than income taxes increased by $11.8 million, from $71.6 million in 2012 to $83.4 million in 2013.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to higher gross receipts tax from higher retail sales as well as an increase in property taxes due to increases in plant and equipment.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UI&#8217;s other income and deductions decreased by $2.3 million, from $20.5 million in 2012 to $18.2 million in 2013.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to the absence in 2013 of the TSO incentive settlement recorded in the third quarter of 2012 partially offset by an increase in allowance for funds used during construction (AFUDC).</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UI&#8217;s interest charges decreased by $2.1 million, from $41.2 million in 2012 to $39.1 million in 2013.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to a reduction in carrying charges on deferred amounts due to customers as well as lower line of credit interest expense.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UI&#8217;s income taxes decreased $6.5 million, from $62.1 million in 2012 to $55.6 million in 2013.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to lower pre-tax income in 2013 compared to 2012, as well as lower non-normalized nuclear stranded cost amortization due to fully amortizing&#160; the CTA in the third quarter of 2013.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Many of the changes in UI&#8217;s unbundled revenue and expense components impact line items in its Consolidated Statement of Income, but do not affect net income, because the costs associated with those components are passed through to customers.&#160; The following discussion details variances which have the most significant impact on net income in the periods presented.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Distribution</u></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The distribution business had total net income of $46.7 million in 2013, a decrease of $6.0 million, compared to 2012.&#160; The decrease was </font>primarily<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> attributable to</font> a one-time pre-tax write off of $8.4 million ($5.0 million after-tax) resulting from disallowances and other adjustments related to the UI&#8217;s rate proceeding as well as increases in employee pension and benefits expense, outside services expenses, depreciation expense and taxes other than income taxes, partially offset by a decrease in rent expense.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Transmission</u></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The transmission business had total net income of $33.6 million in 2013, an increase of $1.7 million, compared to 2012.&#160; The increase was </font>primarily<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> attributable to an increase in the income earned on an increase in rate base as well as an increase in allowance for funds used during construction, partially offset by a $2.6 million pre-tax reserve recorded in the third quarter of 2013 related to a FERC ROE claim.</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Gas Distribution</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gas Companies&#8217; operating revenue increased by $112.1 million, from $702.9 million in 2012 to $815.0 million in 2013.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to higher sales volume from off-system sales, which was largely offset by increased purchased gas expense, as well as the impact of colder weather, increased per customer usage in 2013</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div id="DSPFPageFooter"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">- 45 -</div>

<hr style="BORDER-RIGHT-WIDTH: 0px; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #000000; PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; BORDER-TOP-WIDTH: 0px; BORDER-BOTTOM-WIDTH: 0px; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both; BORDER-LEFT-WIDTH: 0px" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">

</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">compared to 2012, customer growth and increased conservation expense recovery.&#160; Temperatures in 2013 were consistent with normal temperatures but were colder compared to 2012 which resulted in an 18.5% increase in heating degree days in 2013.&#160; The colder temperatures and increased per customer usage in 2013 compared to 2012 resulted in a $20.9 million increase, pre-tax, in gross margin (operating revenues less natural gas purchased) in 2013.&#160; Retail sales increased by 8.3 million mcf, from 69.3 million mcf in 2012, to 77.6 million mcf in 2013.&#160; The customer growth in 2013 compared to 2012 resulted in a $7.0 million increase, pre-tax, in gross margin in 2013.&#160; Fluctuations in natural gas prices have no impact on net income because the cost associated with such variances is passed through to customers.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Purchased gas expense increased by $68.0 million, from $370.2 million in 2012 to $438.2 million in 2013.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to higher sales volume from off-system sales, and colder weather in 2013 compared to 2012.&#160; Fluctuations in natural gas prices have no impact on net income because the cost associated with such variances is passed through to customers.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gas Companies&#8217; O&amp;M expense increased by $16.7 million, from $137.7 million in 2012 to $154.4 million in 2013.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to increased conservation, pension and benefits, and payroll expenses.&#160; Conservation expenses are fully offset by operating revenues.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Depreciation and amortization expense increased by $2.7 million, from $75.2 million in 2012 to $77.9 million in 2013. The increase was primarily attributable to increased depreciation due to increases in plant and equipment.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gas Companies&#8217; taxes other than income taxes increased by $4.2 million, from $42.3 million in 2012 to $46.5 million in 2013.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to higher gross receipts tax due to the increase in operating revenues as well as higher real estate, personal property and sales tax.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gas Companies&#8217; other income and deductions decreased by $4.4 million, from $4.1 million of income in 2012 to $0.3 million of deductions in 2013.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to the decrease in the income related to the weather insurance contracts due to colder temperatures in 2013 compared to 2012.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Income tax expense increased by $2.0 million, from $21.3 million in 2012 to $23.3 million in 2013.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to higher pre-tax income in 2013 compared to 2012, partially offset by lower conservation and payment program costs and lower state income taxes.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Non-Utility</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings retains certain costs, primarily interest expense on holding company debt, at the holding company, or UIL Corporate level, which are not allocated to its subsidiaries.&#160; UIL Corporate incurred net after-tax costs of $10.4 million, or ($0.20) per share, in 2013 compared to net after-tax costs of $13.3 million, or ($0.26) per share, in 2012.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to tax benefits associated with unitary filing requirements for state income taxes, an increase in capitalized interest, and an increase in income earned on UIL Corporate investments that support UIL Holdings.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Electric Distribution and Transmission</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Overall, UI&#8217;s operating revenue decreased by $14.2 million, from $797.7 million in 2011 to $783.5 million in 2012.&#160; Retail revenue decreased $33.0 million, which was primarily attributable to decreases in distribution sales volume resulting from warmer than normal winter temperatures in 2012 compared to 2011.&#160; Retail sales decreased by 145 million kWh, from 5,576 million kWh in 2011, to 5,431 million kWh in 2012.&#160; Retail sales normalized for the weather impact decreased 74 million kWh, from 5,485 million kWh in 2011, to 5,411 million kWh in 2012.&#160; Other revenues increased $18.6 million, which was primarily attributable to higher transmission revenue as well as the net activity of the SBC working capital allowances due to timing differences, partially offset by the net activity of the GSC working capital allowance due to timing differences.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Purchased power expense decreased by $25.6 million, from $180.1 million in 2011 to $154.5 million in 2012.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to decreased prices of procured wholesale power and decreased sales volume, as discussed above.&#160; UI receives electricity to satisfy its standard service and supplier of last resort requirements through fixed&#8209;price purchased power agreements.&#160; The variance does not impact net income as these costs are recovered through the GSC and Bypassable Federally Mandated Congestion Charges portions of UI&#8217;s unbundled retail customer rates.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UI&#8217;s O&amp;M expenses decreased by $26.3 million, from $248.3 million in 2011, to $222.0 million in 2012.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to a decrease in outside services expenses due to decreased maintenance related to certain projects, a decrease in rent expense due to a reduction in office space utilized by UIL Holdings headquarters,&#160; and decreased uncollectible expense, due to a decrease in customer account write-off activity.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UI&#8217;s transmission wholesale expenses increased by $1.5 million, from $78.0 million in 2011 to $79.5 million in 2012.&#160; The increase was </font>primarily<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> attributable to higher regional transmission expenses, of which UI pays a portion based upon its relative load and which are recovered through rates and, as a result, does not impact net income.</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UI&#8217;s depreciation and amortization increased by $7.2 million, from $96.4 million in 2011 to $103.6 million 2012.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to increased depreciation due to increases in plant and equipment.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UI&#8217;s interest expense decreased by $2.5 million, from $43.7 million in 2011 to $41.2 million in 2012.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to a reduction in carrying charges on deferred amounts due to customers, along with the reversal of the interest accrued on an uncertain tax position related to the tax deduction for repairs and maintenance expenses.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UI's income tax expense increased by $18.1 million, from $44.0 million in 2011 to $62.1 million in 2012.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to higher pre-tax income in 2012 compared to 2011, as well as an increase in the effective income tax rate due primarily to <font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">a decrease in the equity portion of</font>&#160;<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">allowance for funds used during construction (AFUDC), which is a flow-through book/tax difference</font>.</div>

<div id="DSPFPageFooter"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">- 47 -</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">UI&#8217;s income from equity investments increased by $4.0 million, from $11.3 million in 2011 to $15.3 million in 2012.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to increased income from the investment in GenConn due to both of GenConn&#8217;s peaking generation projects now participating in the ISO-New England markets.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Many of the changes in UI&#8217;s unbundled revenue and expense components impact line items in its Consolidated Statement of Income, but do not affect net income, because the costs associated with those components are passed through to customers.&#160; The following discussion details variances which have the most significant impact on net income in the periods presented.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Distribution</u></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The distribution business, which </font>includes all electric utility revenue and expenses except for transmission,<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> had total net income of $52.7 million, an increase of $15.1 million, compared to 2011.&#160; The increase in net income was attributable to increased income from the investment in GenConn as well as </font>decreases in outside services, facilities rent and uncollectible expenses.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u>Transmission</u></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The transmission business had total net income of $32.0 million, an increase of $0.7 million, compared to 2011.&#160; The increase was attributable to income earned on an increase in rate base, partially offset by a decrease in AFUDC.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Gas Distribution</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The gas distribution business had net income of $32.2 million, a decrease of $11.6 million, compared to 2011.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to lower sales volume due to the impact of warmer weather and reduced per customer usage in 2012 compared to 2011.&#160; The warmer temperatures and reduced per customer usage in 2012 compared to 2011 resulted in a $11.1 million decrease, pre-tax, in gross margin (operating revenues less natural gas purchased) in 2012 compared to 2011.&#160; The decrease in net income was partially offset by a decrease in interest expense.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gas Companies&#8217; operating revenue decreased by $69.4 million, from $772.3 million in 2011 to $702.9 million in 2012.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to lower sales volume due to warmer weather.&#160; Retail sales decreased by 2.9 million mcf, from 72.2 million mcf in 2011, to 69.3 million mcf in 2012.&#160; Temperatures were warmer in 2012 compared to 2011 which resulted in 10.8% fewer heating degree days.&#160; Compared to normal temperatures for 2012, there was 16.4% fewer heating degree days.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Purchased gas expense decreased by $58.9 million, from $429.1 million in 2011 to $370.2 million in 2012.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to lower sales volume due to warmer weather.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gas Companies&#8217; O&amp;M expense increased by $4.6 million, from $133.1 million in 2011 to $137.7 million in 2012.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to increased general and administrative expenses primarily due to increased shared services costs and increased uncollectible expenses primarily due to increased customer account write&#8209;off activity.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gas Companies&#8217; depreciation and amortization increased by $4.5 million, from $70.7 million in 2011 to $75.2 million 2012.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to the implementation of new depreciation and amortization rates resulting from the settlement of rate case appeals, which became effective in August 2011, and to increased investment in plant and equipment.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gas Companies&#8217; taxes other than income taxes decreased by $1.2 million, from $43.5 million in 2011 to $42.3 million in 2012.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to lower gross receipts tax due to the decrease in operating revenues.</div>

<div id="DSPFPageFooter"></div>

<hr style="BORDER-RIGHT-WIDTH: 0px; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #000000; PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; BORDER-TOP-WIDTH: 0px; BORDER-BOTTOM-WIDTH: 0px; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both; BORDER-LEFT-WIDTH: 0px" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gas Companies&#8217; other income and deductions decreased by $2.5 million, from $6.6 million in 2011 to $4.1 million in 2012.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to the absence in 2012 of a non-recurring adjustment recorded in 2011 related to carrying charges resulting from the settlement of rate case appeals.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Income tax expense decreased by $8.4 million, from $29.7 million in 2011 to $21.3 million in 2012.&#160; The decrease was primarily attributable to lower pre-tax income in 2012 compared to 2011, as well as to costs associated with customer conservation and payment programs.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Non-Utility</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings retains certain costs, primarily interest expense on holding company debt, at the holding company, or UIL Holdings Corporate level, which are not allocated to its various subsidiaries.&#160; UIL Corporate incurred net after-tax costs of $13.3 million, or $0.26 per share, in 2012 compared to net after-tax costs of $13.0 million, or $0.26 per share, in 2011.</div>

<td style="WIDTH: 36pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; align: right">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="Item7A."><!--Anchor--></a>Item 7A.</div>
</td>
<td style="WIDTH: auto; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; align: left">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk.</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following discussion details the primary market risks applicable to UIL Holdings and its subsidiaries.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">UIL Holdings faces the risks that UIL Holdings and its subsidiaries will not be able to access the bank and/or debt and equity capital markets or be able to access these markets on favorable terms to refinance debt as it matures, to remarket debt in the municipal bond market, to issue new debt or equity to support capital requirements, or to secure bank credit facilities to provide sufficient liquidity.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There has been considerable dislocation in the auction rate municipal bond market, and there have been failed auctions, resulting from insufficient clearing bids.&#160; Among the failed auctions were the auctions for the $64.5 million principal amount of auction rate bonds.&#160; When there are insufficient clearing bids as a result of an auction, the interest rates are set at a rate equal to one-month LIBOR times a multiple of 125% to 225%, based on the credit rating on the auction rate bonds assigned by Moody&#8217;s or S&amp;P.&#160; The principal and interest payments on $64.5 million principal amount of tax-exempt auction rate bonds are insured by Ambac Assurance Corporation (Ambac), but the bonds are currently rated based on Moody&#8217;s underlying credit rating of UI of Baa1.&#160; In the event of subsequent failed auctions of these bonds, the interest rate will continue to be reset as described above.&#160; The interest rate on these bonds was 0.310% at February 10, 2014 which was equal to two times LIBOR.&#160; The interest rate risk of variable rate financings, including the reset at auction of the interest rate on this $64.5 million principal amount of auction rate bonds, is $0.2 million of increased interest expense for every 0.25% increase in interest rates.&#160; UI continues to review conditions in the municipal bond market and plans to refund the $64.5 million principal amount of these bonds, at such time when market conditions and financing terms are economically favorable.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The 4.50% Series 2010 notes, due July 1, 2027 in the principal amount outstanding of $27.5 million, are due to be remarketed in the municipal bond market on July 1, 2015.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The weighted-average remaining fixed rate period of outstanding long-term debt obligations of UIL Holdings and its subsidiaries as of December 31, 2013 was 11.7 years, at an average interest rate of 5.44%.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The short-term borrowing costs of UIL Holdings and its subsidiaries fluctuate with the upward and downward movements of LIBOR, <font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">JPMorgan Chase Bank&#8217;s prime rate and the Federal Funds Rate (as defined in the short-term credit facility of UIL Holdings and its subsidiaries described </font>in Part II, Item 8. &#8220;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> &#8211; </font>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements&#8221;<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> &#8211; </font>Note (D) &#8220;Short&#8209;Term Credit Arrangements&#8221; of this Form 10-K<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">, respectively).</font>&#160; Rates associated with the money market loan arrangement that UIL Holdings has with JPMorgan Chase Bank fluctuate based on rates in the money market.&#160; Such rates are influenced by financial market conditions and the actions of the Federal Reserve.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition, UI requires that its energy suppliers provide performance security to guarantee performance under contracts for standard service and supplier of last resort service.&#160; Specifically, UI requires wholesale suppliers to provide both parent guarantees and letters of credit.&#160; This performance assurance is intended to allow UI to recover for its customers the cost of replacement power, as well as administrative and legal costs, associated with a supplier default.</div>
